rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 report own data from a 3.3 ha pilot vineyard in Marche (airborne thermal surveys with CWSI maps, Bioristor in vivo sensors, Sentek multilevel soil water probes, cost questionnaire, WP/EWP indices).
rows.notes: The study does not report any result of sensors delivering water use efficiency or water savings. The vineyard has no irrigation system (Section 2.1 and Conclusions state this as a limitation); no irrigation was applied or scheduled using sensor data. Soil probes (Sentek) are used only to compare with Bioristor response (Section 3.3, Figure 10). WP for 2021 'with irrigation' (Table 4) is an estimate based on hypothetical irrigation and estimated yield, and it actually decreases with irrigation. The study shows that sensors (thermal CWSI, Bioristor, soil probe) can detect/map water stress - a precondition of optimizing irrigation, not the claimed effect. The sensors emphasised are thermal imaging and the Bioristor sap sensor rather than soil moisture sensors specifically.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 report own measurements (thermal surveys, Bioristor and soil-probe time series, farm cost questionnaire, yields in Table 3).
rows.notes: No own result on sensors maintaining or improving grape yield or quality. No sensor-guided irrigation was performed; the observed 2021 yield (86 q/ha vs 113 in 2020) fell due to drought, and the 103 q/ha 'with irrigation' figure in Table 3 is an estimate of what would have happened had the winery irrigated in response to sensor-detected stress (Section 3.4), not a measured outcome. Grape quality was not measured. The study only shows detection of water stress periods (Bioristor, CWSI maps; Section 3.3 notes stress impacted flowering and veraison) and suggests irrigation could have been scheduled - a precondition of the claimed yield/quality effect. Soil moisture probes themselves play a minor comparative role.

notes: Study is a descriptive case study of a prototype platform plus sensors and an economic simulation in a non-irrigated vineyard; it contains no trial of sensor-based irrigation and therefore no outcome evidence on water use efficiency or yield/quality. Text appears complete; some figure captions duplicated by PDF extraction.
